t: Section 2423(b) of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking “2245” and inserting “2246”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical conforming amendment that changes a cross-reference number in a criminal statute. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for any party outside the federal government, so there is no participation.
fable.s: is amended by striking “2245” and inserting “2246”

opus.w: The section only swaps one cross-reference number for another in a criminal statute. It brings no one from outside the federal government into a federal decision, and it creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Nothing in it is even on-topic for participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a criminal statute, correcting a cross-reference number. It does not establish any process for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. It involves no advisory committees, public hearings, comment periods, or rights to sue. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 2423(b) of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking “2245” and inserting “2246”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute is a "decision" and that the amendment process involves Congress (inside government), so it's "No". However, the text itself contains no mechanism for outside participation; it is merely a technical correction of a cross-reference. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory board mentioned. The text is purely legislative housekeeping.
